steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on mask-based pretraining for generalizable neural radiance fields (masked ray and view modeling). Motivate generalizable NeRF, connect it to masked modeling in NLP and vision, describe our method at a high level, and list the contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- NeRF and the need for generalizable NeRF
- Unused correlations among sampled features; lessons from masked modeling (MLM, MIM)
- Proposed method: masked ray and view modeling (MRVM)
- Experiments and contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:

  - Generalizable NeRF (cite): one model for various scenes, applied directly to unseen scene at inference
- Correlations + masked modeling
  - existing generalizable NeRF: sample image features from several visible reference views as conditions
  - correlations among sampled features not well exploited
  - MLM (cite) in NLP, MIM (cite) in CV: mask-then-predict, mask a proportion, predict missing info from rest
  - learns high-level global representation, helps downstream tasks
  - for NeRF: global info from mask-based pretraining = "3D scene prior knowledge", very useful for generalizable NeRF
  - novel scene: helps reconstruct high-quality scene from limited reference views
- MRVM
  - masked ray and view modeling, tailored for NeRF; natural correlations among points along rays + across reference views
  - pretraining objective: predict complete scene representations from partially masked ones (along rays, across views)
  - NeRF implicit -> predictive pretraining in latent space, motivated by prior work (cite); optimized jointly with rendering task
  - after pretraining: finetune across scenes or on a specific scene
  - simple, efficient, model-agnostic; applicable to various generalizable NeRF models
- Experiments + contributions
  - large-scale synthetic datasets + challenging real-world datasets; MLP-based and transformer-based architectures
  - quantitative + qualitative: better generalizability, more precise geometry, richer texture
  - contrib 1: 3D implicit representation learning improved by mask-based modeling like MLM/MIM if inner correlations used right
  - contrib 2: MRVM-NeRF, simple efficient self-supervised pretraining objective; first mask-based pretraining in NeRF field
  - contrib 3: extensive experiments, various datasets + backbones; effectiveness + general applicability

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) has become a powerful tool for 3D scene reconstruction and generation. Most NeRF-based methods can render striking visual results, but they are still restricted to one particular static scene, which limits where they can be applied. Recent works study Generalizable NeRF so that various scenes can be modeled with a single model, which can then be applied directly to an unseen scene at inference.

Most existing methods for generalizable NeRF sample image features from several visible reference views and use them as the conditions for learning scene representations. But the correlations among these sampled features have not been exploited well before. Earlier masked modeling tasks, like masked language modeling (MLM) in natural language processing and masked image modeling (MIM) in computer vision, exploit such correlations among input signals with a mask-then-predict task: they mask out a proportion of the inputs and try to predict the missing information from the rest. This way a high-level global representation can be learned, which helps downstream tasks. For NeRFs, we find that the high-level global information learned with mask-based pretraining, which we call the 3D scene prior knowledge, is also very useful for generalizable Neural Radiance Field. When it is applied to a novel scene, this prior knowledge helps reconstruct a high-quality new scene from limited reference views.

- MRVM
  - masked ray and view modeling, tailored for NeRF; natural correlations among points along rays + across reference views
  - pretraining objective: predict complete scene representations from partially masked ones (along rays, across views)
  - NeRF implicit -> predictive pretraining in latent space, motivated by prior work; optimized jointly with rendering task
  - after pretraining: finetune across scenes or on a specific scene
  - simple, efficient, model-agnostic; applicable to various generalizable NeRF models

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) has become a powerful tool for 3D scene reconstruction and generation. Most NeRF-based methods can render striking visual results, but they are still restricted to one particular static scene, which limits where they can be applied. Recent works study Generalizable NeRF so that various scenes can be modeled with a single model, which can then be applied directly to an unseen scene at inference.

Most existing methods for generalizable NeRF sample image features from several visible reference views and use them as the conditions for learning scene representations. But the correlations among these sampled features have not been exploited well before. Earlier masked modeling tasks, like masked language modeling (MLM) in natural language processing and masked image modeling (MIM) in computer vision, exploit such correlations among input signals with a mask-then-predict task: they mask out a proportion of the inputs and try to predict the missing information from the rest. This way a high-level global representation can be learned, which helps downstream tasks. For NeRFs, we find that the high-level global information learned with mask-based pretraining, which we call the 3D scene prior knowledge, is also very useful for generalizable Neural Radiance Field. When it is applied to a novel scene, this prior knowledge helps reconstruct a high-quality new scene from limited reference views.

So we propose masked ray and view modeling (MRVM), which is tailored for NeRF, since there are naturally correlations among the sampled points along rays and across the reference views. Specifically, we introduce a pretraining objective that predicts the complete scene representations from ones that are partially masked along rays and across views, to encourage inner interactions at these two levels. Because NeRFs are implicit representations, and motivated by prior work, we do our predictive pretraining in the latent space and optimize it together with the original rendering task of NeRF. After the generalizable NeRF model is pretrained with MRVM, it is finetuned either across various scenes or on a specific scene. This simple but efficient masked modeling design is model-agnostic, in the sense that it can be applied widely to various generalizable NeRF models.

To show that MRVM is effective and widely applicable, we run extensive experiments on commonly used large-scale synthetic datasets and on more challenging real-world realistic datasets, with both MLP-based and transformer-based network architectures. Quantitative and qualitative results show that masked ray and view modeling significantly improves the generalizability of NeRF, rendering more precise geometric structures and richer texture details. Our contributions are:

- We find that 3D implicit representation learning can be significantly improved by mask-based modeling like MLM and MIM, if the inner correlations of 3D scene representations are used in the right way.

- We present a simple but efficient self-supervised pretraining objective for generalizable NeRF, called MRVM-NeRF. As far as we know, it is the first attempt to bring mask-based pretraining into the NeRF field.

- We run extensive experiments on various synthetic and real-world datasets with different backbones. The results show the effectiveness and general applicability of our masked ray and view modeling.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) [1] has emerged as a powerful tool for 3D scene reconstruction [2,3,4] and generation [5,6,7]. Though most NeRF-based methods can render striking visual results, they are still restricted to a particular static scene, which limits their application. Recent works study Generalizable NeRF [8,9,10,11,12] to model various scenes with a single model, which can be directly applied to an unseen scene during inference.

Most existing methods for generalizable NeRF sample image features from several visible reference views as the conditions for learning scene representations. However, the correlations among the sampled features have not been well exploited before. Previous masked modeling tasks, including masked language modeling (MLM) [13] in natural language processing and masked image modeling (MIM) [14,13,15,16] in computer vision, exploit such correlations among input signals through a mask-then-predict task: masking out a proportion of the inputs and trying to predict the missing information from the remaining ones. In this way, a high-level global representation can be learned, which is beneficial for downstream tasks. For NeRFs, we find that the high-level global information learned through mask-based pretraining, which we call the 3D scene prior knowledge, is also extremely useful for generalizable Neural Radiance Field. When applied to a novel scene, such prior knowledge helps reconstruct a high-quality new scene from limited reference views.

To this end, we propose masked ray and view modeling (MRVM) tailored for NeRF, considering that there are naturally correlations among the sampled points along rays and across the reference views. Specifically, we introduce a pretraining objective to predict the complete scene representations from ones that are partially masked along rays and across views, aiming to encourage inner interactions at the two levels. Given that NeRFs are implicit representations, and motivated by [17,18], we conduct our predictive pretraining in the latent space and optimize it together with NeRF's original rendering task. After pretraining the generalizable NeRF model with MRVM, the model is further finetuned either across various scenes or on a specific scene. Such a simple yet efficient masked modeling design is model-agnostic, in the sense that it is widely applicable to various generalizable NeRF models.

To demonstrate the effectiveness and wide applicability of MRVM, we conduct extensive experiments on both commonly used large-scale synthetic datasets and more challenging real-world realistic datasets, based on both MLP-based and transformer-based network architectures. Quantitative and qualitative results show that our masked ray and view modeling significantly improves the generalizability of NeRF, rendering more precise geometric structures and richer texture details. Our contributions can be summarized as follows:

- • We find that 3D implicit representation learning can be significantly improved by mask-based modeling as in MLM and MIM, when the inner correlations of 3D scene representations are harnessed in the right manner.

- • We present a simple yet efficient self-supervised pretraining objective for generalizable NeRF, termed MRVM-NeRF. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first attempt to incorporate mask-based pretraining into the NeRF field.

- • We conduct extensive experiments on various synthetic and real-world datasets with different backbones. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and general applicability of our masked ray and view modeling.
